mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship holds consistently across monetary policy regimes.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day S&P 500 returns is negative or below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return in low-FEDFUNDS periods (FEDFUNDS < 0.25%) is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 0.1 percentage points from the prior month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return when UNRATE rises > 0.1pp from prior month is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05), or the Rank IC for the UNRATE change as a predictor is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) above 0.5% from the prior month signals robust consumer demand, which supports corporate earnings growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both rise > 0.5% from prior month
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return when both HOUST and RSAFS rise > 0.5% from prior month is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05), or the Rank IC for the interaction term (HOUST_change * RSAFS_change) is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of industrial production contraction (INDPRO below its 12-month moving average), the market prices in reduced corporate output and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return when INDPRO < 12-month moving average is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05), or the Rank IC for INDPRO as a predictor in contraction regimes is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the CPI index above 0.2% signals rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 5-day forward return when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.2% from prior month is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05), or the Rank IC for CPIAUCSL change is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong labor market expansion (PAYEMS growth exceeding 100,000 jobs per month), corporate hiring supports consumer spending and earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 60-day forward return when PAYEMS growth > 100k per month is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05), or the Rank IC for PAYEMS growth as a predictor is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly housing starts level above 550,000 units signals strong residential construction activity, which boosts related sectors and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 5-day forward return when HOUST > 550 is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05), or the Rank IC for HOUST as a predictor is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of severe industrial contraction (INDPRO below 90), the market prices in a deep recession, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 60-day forward return when INDPRO < 90 is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05), or the Rank IC for INDPRO as a predictor in severe contraction regimes is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
